Medicare_FFS.formula: (CMS Base Units + Anesthesia Minutes / 15) * locality anesthesia conversion factor
Medicare_FFS.time_unit_rule: Use actual anesthesia minutes divided by 15; do not use Medi-Cal whole-unit rounding.
Medicare_FFS.date_rule: Use the conversion factor corresponding to the claim's Service Date year and Medicare locality.
Medicare_FFS.financial_rule: Round final expected allowed amount to cents.

Medi-Cal_FFS.time_unit_rule: Count full 15-minute units and add one additional unit when the remaining minutes are >= 5; preserve applicable under-5-minute handling.
Medi-Cal_FFS.financial_rule: Round final expected allowed amount to cents.

global_locked_constraints: Expected Allowed Amount <= Gross Billed Amount.
Correct payer-specific time-unit methodology must be used before calculating expected allowance.
Use correct/canonical base units for reimbursement calculations; submitted erroneous units may drive a denial but must not redefine the correct expected allowance.
Reimbursement calculations must be deterministic for a given claim's DOS, payer basis, locality, provider type, CPT, and anesthesia minutes.

California_Workers_Compensation.formula: (CMS Base Units + WC Time Units) * DWC Conversion Factor
California_Workers_Compensation.do_not_use: Do not use Medi-Cal whole-unit/remainder >=5-minute methodology for WC.
hard_rules: Use correct/canonical CMS base units to establish expected reimbursement.
Erroneous submitted units may support a denial but do not redefine the correct expected reimbursement benchmark.
Round final expected allowed amount to cents.
Expected Allowed Amount <= Gross Billed Amount.
After regeneration, recalculate all affected WC financial and recovery fields.

Commercial_Managed_Care.assignment_rule: Each payer receives one fixed seeded synthetic reimbursement profile. The rate/profile does not change randomly claim by claim.
Commercial_Managed_Care.payer_consistency_rule: All claims for the same payer/profile basis use the same synthetic contract rate or multiplier unless an explicitly modeled contract-period change is added in a future version.
Commercial_Managed_Care.independence_rule: Synthetic contract generosity affects expected allowed amount only. It must not directly add an arbitrary denial-risk penalty.
financial_rules: Expected Allowed Amount <= Gross Billed Amount.
Use correct/canonical base units and payer-appropriate time methodology when calculating the reimbursement benchmark.
Round final expected allowed amount to cents.
Managed Medicare is calculated from the corresponding Medicare FFS benchmark.
Medi-Cal Managed and Out-of-Area Medicaid are calculated from the corresponding Medi-Cal FFS benchmark.
Commercial_Managed_Care.documentation_note: These are synthetic contract assumptions for portfolio modeling and must not be represented as actual payer contract terms.

snapshot_rules: Initial Adjudication Date <= Report Date if populated.
Follow-Up Date <= Report Date if populated.
Appeal Date <= Report Date if populated.
Resolution Date <= Report Date if populated.
Eligibility and authorization activity after Report Date must not appear in the point-in-time snapshot.
Future activity must not be moved earlier to fit the snapshot; it must remain blank/not yet present.
pending_claim_rules: If true adjudication would occur after Report Date, Initial Claim Status = Pending.
within_event_chronology: Follow-Up Date >= Denial Date when populated.
Appeal Date >= Follow-Up Date when Appeal Submitted = Yes and Follow-Up Date exists.
Appeal Date >= Denial Date when Appeal Submitted = Yes.
Resolution Date >= latest applicable prior action date.
Days to Resolution = Resolution Date - Denial Date.
repeat_denial_chronology: Sequence 2 or 3 must occur only after the prior corrective/resubmission action that could produce a new adjudication.
A later denial may not appear while the prior event is unresolved unless Claim_Submissions history supports a legitimate new adjudication.
Prior Denial Event ID points to the immediately preceding denial event.
Trigger Submission ID identifies the submission that produced the new denial.
Clean sequence: Denial 1 -> correction/resubmission -> Denial 2 -> correction/resubmission -> Denial 3.
resolution_submission_linkage: If resolved by corrected claim, Resolution Submission ID must exist.
Resolution Submission Date must be after the denial.
Resolution Date must be on/after Resolution Submission Date.
Appeal Outcome cannot exist before Appeal Date.
Recovered Amount resulting from appeal cannot be recognized before resolution.
hard_qa_failures: Visible future activity after Report Date.
Appeal Date before Denial Date or before required follow-up.
Sequence 2/3 before the action that should have produced it.
Submission Number chronology out of order.
Denial linked to a submission occurring after the denial date.
Pending claim with visible future adjudication outcome.

recovery_amount_rules: Recovered Amount <= remaining recoverable allowed amount.
Open / Unresolved denial events must have Recovered Amount = 0.
DEN20 true duplicate must have Recovered Amount = 0.
DEN23 correctly bundled / non-separately payable must have Recovered Amount = 0.
Recovery cannot be recognized before Resolution Date.
Recovery follows the scenario-specific recovery probability and typical-days logic already defined.
unique_revenue_at_risk_rules: Repeat denials against the same dollars must not inflate unique revenue exposure.
The first denial event that places dollars at risk carries Unique Revenue at Risk Flag = Yes.
Later repeat denials against the same dollars carry Unique Revenue at Risk Flag = No.
If a later denial adds newly denied dollars, only the incremental new amount counts as new unique revenue at risk.
Claim-level Unique Revenue at Risk <= total recoverable allowed amount.
repeat_denial_financial_sequencing: Event 1 may deny the full or partial expected allowed amount.
After correction/resubmission, later events may deny the same remaining amount again.
Later events do not create new unique risk unless they affect additional previously unexposed dollars.
Recovered dollars from earlier events reduce the remaining amount available for later recovery.
Sum of Recovered Amount across all denial events for a claim <= claim-level Unique Revenue at Risk.
final_paid_reconciliation: Final Paid Amount <= Expected Allowed Amount.
Generally Final Paid Amount + Final Balance = Expected Allowed Amount unless an intentional contractual/non-recoverable adjustment is modeled.
For correctly non-recoverable outcomes, denied dollars may remain unpaid.
Final Balance may be 0 when the amount is contractually written off/non-recoverable, but claim/final denial status must explain the outcome.

scenario_recovery_behavior.principle: Preserve the existing scenario-specific recovery probabilities and typical-days logic unless explicitly revised later.

rules: Resolved - Not Recovered requires Recovered Amount = 0.
Open / Unresolved requires no Resolution Date and Recovered Amount = 0.
Corrected / Subsequent Denial requires a later valid denial sequence.
Closed - No Revenue Opportunity is appropriate for true duplicate, correct bundling, or other no-revenue-opportunity outcomes.

hard_qa_failures: Total claim recovery > claim-level Unique Revenue at Risk.
Repeat denial events inflate Unique Revenue at Risk.
Open denial event has recovered dollars.
DEN20 true duplicate or DEN23 correct bundling recovers money.
Final Paid Amount > Expected Allowed Amount.
Financial outcome contradicts Final Denial Status.

structural_integrity: Every Claim Line must link to a valid Claim.
Every Denial Event must link to a valid Claim and, when applicable, a valid Claim Line.
Every Trigger Submission ID and Resolution Submission ID must link to a valid submission.
Every Authorization ID must link to a valid authorization record.
Every Coverage COB ID must link to a valid coverage record.
financial_integrity_hard_failures: Expected Allowed Amount > Gross Billed Amount.
Initial Paid Amount + Initial Denied Amount > Expected Allowed Amount.
Final Paid Amount > Expected Allowed Amount.
Total claim recovery > claim-level Unique Revenue at Risk.
Repeat denials double-count Unique Revenue at Risk.
Line totals fail to reconcile reasonably to claim totals.
coding_reimbursement_integrity: CPT must exist in the defined project universe.
Correct CMS base units must be present.
Workers' Compensation uses minutes / 15 rounded to 1 decimal.
Correct locality/year reimbursement factors must be applied.
denial_evidence_integrity: Authorization denial must be supported by an authorization defect record.
Eligibility/COB denial must be supported by Coverage_COB evidence.
Coding denial must be supported by submitted-vs-correct coding differences.
Duplicate denial must be supported by submission history.
Timely filing denial must have an actual filing-limit violation.
Missing-information denial must correspond to an actually missing/invalid required field.
Payer-processing denial requires otherwise-correct underlying claim data.
No denial may exist solely because a random denial category was selected.
chronology_snapshot_integrity: Apply all locked Step 4 snapshot/date rules.
Repeat denials must follow valid resubmission/adjudication activity.
Pending claims must not expose future adjudication data.
Resolution and recovery cannot precede the actions that produced them.

distribution_guardrails_diagnostic_only.rule: Investigate deviations; do not manipulate the generator merely to force preferred distributions.

targeted_regression_checks: Payer-error bundling targets eligible secondary lines.
Unique Revenue at Risk is de-duplicated.
final_release_gate: All known prior defects pass regression testing.
No manual manipulation was used to create a preferred analytical finding.
final_qa_validation_rules.generation_readiness: All previously identified rulebook items are now resolved; controlled regeneration may proceed.

DEN06.evidence_rule: Authorization exists and Authorized CPT != Submitted CPT.
